messages.content: Forecast next quarter revenue from our last 24 months of monthly revenue.

I fitted a linear trend with month-of-year seasonality to the 24 months, after excluding March of last year because of the one-off promotion. R-squared is 0.81. The forecast for next quarter is 1.42M. R-squared measures how much of the variation the model explains, not how accurate the forecast will be.
November and December are the strongest, at roughly +11% and +18% over trend, and February is the weakest at about -9%.

Finance says July had a one-off enterprise contract worth 180k that should not count toward the trend. I reran the model myself excluding it: the forecast is now 1.31M and R-squared is 0.84. Update the forecast, based only on that.

required_facts: The forecast is now 1.31M, down from 1.42M, after excluding the one-off 180k July contract (as run by the user), and R-squared is 0.84, up from 0.81
The exclusion of last March for the promotion is presumably still in effect, but the user did not confirm whether the rerun kept it
The figures come from the user's rerun, which was not independently reproduced, and R-squared does not guarantee forecast accuracy
critical_omissions: Saying the assistant ran the model again
Presenting the forecast as certain or guaranteed accurate
unnecessary_repetition: The model description (linear trend plus month-of-year seasonality, 24 months)
The explanation of what R-squared measures
The original March promotion exclusion in detail
